A mature medium-to-large sturdy athletic Borador, named Labrador Retriever–Border Collie cross, with developed broad skull and moderately broad strong tapering muzzle, black nose, ordinary brown eyes and natural medium triangular folded drop ears. Proportional neck, broad firm back, moderately deep chest and slight abdominal tuck; body modestly longer than tall, robust well-proportioned muscular limbs and compact natural paws. Short reasonably coarse glossy black coat, with an independently chosen small white chest patch and restrained white toe marks, no merle. Complete thick-based gradually tapering full natural tail with modest fur, hanging backward/down in relaxed stance with slight open upward bend near free tip; not docked or a tight overback curl. Variable cross appearance acknowledged, selected evidence-supported interpretation only; not parental trait averaging or a uniform breed ideal.

profileEvidence.summary: Energetic and attentive to their people, Boradors often enjoy a job to do as well as close companionship. They can be keen learners and vocal watchdogs, though an individual’s temperament varies. This Labrador Retriever–Border Collie cross varies in size and coat, with no single fixed look.
